en: a. having a strong, hot flavor because of spices; containing a lot of spices; (of a story or joke) slightly rude or exciting; full of excitement
ex: I like spicy food like Sichuan hot pot.
我喜歡四川麻辣鍋這類辛辣食物。

en: n. a story or an account of events; the way in which a story is told; the process of telling a story; a. relating to a story or the telling of a story
ex: The book is a powerful narrative about war and peace.
這本書是關於戰爭與和平的有力敘事。

en: a. using words; spoken and not written; relating to verbs; word for word; connected with the use of words
ex: We had a verbal agreement but nothing was written down.
我們有口頭協議，但沒有書面紀錄。

en: n. a description of possible events or a possible situation; a written outline of a film or play; a plan of what might happen; a situation that might exist
ex: The worst-case scenario is that we lose all our data.
最糟的情況是我們失去所有資料。

en: n. financial support given by a company or person to an event, team or person; the state of being supported by a sponsor; the act of providing support; the role of a godparent
ex: The race was held with sponsorship from a local company.
這場比賽由當地一家公司贊助舉辦。

en: n. sports activities such as running, jumping and throwing; sports in general, especially those played at school; (British) a group of sports including running and jumping
ex: She won a gold medal in athletics at the Olympics.
她在奧運田徑項目中贏得金牌。

en: a. making you feel sad because someone is weak or in a bad situation; very poor or weak; (informal) very bad or useless; causing pity
ex: It was a pathetic attempt to cover up the mistake.
那是個拙劣的掩蓋錯誤的嘗試。

en: n. the ideas, attitudes or activities that are accepted by most people; the main current of a river; a. relating to ideas that are accepted by most people
ex: The film appeals to mainstream audiences.
這部電影吸引主流觀眾。

en: a. feeling sad and without hope; making you feel sad and without hope; dark and unpleasant; (of a place) dark in a way that makes you feel unhappy
ex: The weather was gloomy and gray all week.
整個星期天氣都陰沉灰暗。

en: n. an important event in the development of something; a stone that marks the distance in miles along a road; an important stage in a process; a significant event or achievement
ex: The birth of their first child was an important milestone in their lives.
第一個孩子的誕生是他們人生的重要里程碑。

en: n. an official document that gives someone the sole right to make or sell an invention; the right to make or sell a new invention; a. obvious or clear; (of a product) protected by a patent; vt. to get a patent for an invention
ex: The company applied for a patent on its new design.
公司為新設計申請了專利。

en: n. a formal and serious discussion of a subject; a long speech or piece of writing about a subject; a way of using language; vi. to speak or write about a subject at length
ex: The professor gave a long discourse on modern philosophy.
教授針對現代哲學發表了一長篇論述。

en: n. a meeting of people for a social or a particular purpose; the act of collecting things; the act of coming together in a group
ex: The family held a small gathering to celebrate her birthday.
家人辦了一場小聚會來慶祝她的生日。

en: vi. to develop gradually over a long period of time; (of animals and plants) to change slowly over many generations; vt. to develop something gradually; to create something over time
ex: Birds evolved from dinosaurs millions of years ago.
鳥類在數百萬年前從恐龍演化而來。

en: n. an elected official in a county who is in charge of law enforcement; (in the United States) an officer who enforces the law in a county; (in England) the chief officer of a county
ex: The sheriff arrested the robber in the small town.
治安官在小鎮上逮捕了搶匪。

en: n. the interests or benefit of someone; used in the phrase on behalf of to mean acting for someone else; the support or advantage of someone
ex: I am writing on behalf of the whole class.
我代表全班寫這封信。

en: n. a person who has the legal right to receive property or a title when the owner dies; a person who continues the work or ideas of someone else; a successor
ex: The prince is the heir to the throne.
王子是王位的繼承人。

en: vt. to start something such as a plan or process; to introduce someone to a new activity or a secret society; n. a person who has recently been admitted to a group or organization; a. newly admitted
ex: The government initiated a new program to help the poor.
政府發起了一項幫助窮人的新計畫。

en: n. the process of being slowly destroyed by natural processes; the state of becoming worse over time; the loss of quality or strength; v. to be gradually destroyed by bacteria; to become worse over time
ex: Tooth decay can be prevented by brushing regularly.
經常刷牙可以預防蛀牙。

en: n. a person who watches television; a person who looks at something; a device for looking at photographs or films; a person who watches a performance
ex: Millions of viewers watched the final match on television.
數百萬名觀眾透過電視觀看了決賽。

en: n. an unreasonable dislike or preference that is not based on facts; a feeling against a person or group because of their race, religion or sex; vt. to influence someone or something in an unfair way; to cause harm to someone or something
ex: She fought against racial prejudice all her life.
她一輩子都在對抗種族偏見。

en: a. very great or very deep; showing great knowledge or understanding; having a very strong effect on someone; (of a feeling) felt very strongly
ex: The book had a profound effect on her thinking.
這本書對她的思想產生了深遠的影響。

en: a. large in amount or important; strongly built; having real value or importance; (of a meal) large and satisfying; n. an important material or thing
ex: The company made a substantial profit last year.
公司去年賺了可觀的利潤。

en: n. the legal status of being a member of a country; the state of being a member of a country or a city; the rights and responsibilities of being a citizen; the condition of belonging to a particular country
ex: She applied for Canadian citizenship after living there for five years.
她在加拿大住了五年後申請入籍。

en: n. a small shop or open-fronted booth in a market; a place for one animal in a barn; the act of stopping an engine; a delaying tactic; vt. to stop an engine; to put an animal in a stall; to delay someone; vi. (of an engine) to stop; to avoid giving a direct answer
ex: He runs a fruit stall at the market.
他在市場經營一個水果攤。

en: n. the act of putting something in a particular place; the act of finding a job or place for someone; the place or position where something is put; a short period of work for students; a student's level in a class
ex: The school helps graduates with job placement.
學校協助畢業生就業安置。

en: n. a person who takes direct action to bring about a social or political change; a person who actively campaigns for a cause; a person who believes in using strong action
ex: Environmental activists protested outside the factory.
環保人士在工廠外抗議。

en: n. a group of things made or dealt with at one time; a quantity of bread or cakes baked at one time; a number of computer jobs handled together; v. to process things in a group
ex: She baked a batch of cookies for the party.
她為派對烤了一批餅乾。

en: a. very famous and admired; existing only in legends; (of a person) very well known for a particular quality; known as a figure in an old story
ex: Michael Jordan is a legendary basketball player.
麥可喬丹是傳奇的籃球運動員。

en: n. a narrow and very strong beam of light, used for cutting, in medicine and in communication; a device that produces such a beam; a type of device used in surgery
ex: Doctors used a laser to treat his eye condition.
醫生用雷射治療他的眼疾。

en: n. a situation in which you have to make a difficult choice between two things; a difficult problem with no easy answer; a situation where two alternatives are both bad
ex: She faced a dilemma between family and career.
她面臨家庭與事業之間的兩難。
ph: on the horns of a dilemma

en: n. an official document that proves that you have completed a course, passed a test or have a particular qualification; a document that states the truth of something; vt. to give someone an official document that confirms something
ex: Each student received a certificate at the end of the course.
每位學生在課程結束時都拿到了證書。

en: vt. to become aware of something by using your senses; to understand something in a particular way; to notice something that is not obvious; vi. to be aware of things
ex: She perceived a change in his behavior.
她察覺到他的行為有所改變。

en: n. a bar of wood or metal used to hang something on; a fence or barrier; a metal track on which trains run; a means of travel by train; a small bird that lives near water; vt. to put a bar around something; vi. to complain angrily
ex: He leaned on the rail of the balcony and looked at the view.
他倚著陽台的欄杆望向風景。

en: n. the close watching of a person or place, especially by the police or army; the act of observing someone or something carefully; the act of watching for a long time
ex: The airport uses video surveillance to keep passengers safe.
機場使用影像監視來確保旅客安全。

en: a. relating to a system of government in which several states are joined together under a central government; relating to the central government of a country; formed by the joining of separate states
ex: The federal government plans to raise taxes next year.
聯邦政府計畫明年提高稅收。

en: a. based on truth or reason and therefore accepted; (of a document) legally acceptable; (of a ticket or passport) able to be used; (of an argument) logical and correct
ex: You need a valid passport to travel abroad.
出國旅行需要有效的護照。

en: vt. to formally tell someone about something; to officially inform someone; to give a person official information about something
ex: Please notify us if you change your address.
如果你更改地址，請通知我們。

en: n. the crime of getting money by deceiving people; a person who pretends to be someone else to deceive people; a trick that is intended to cheat someone
ex: He was arrested for credit card fraud.
他因信用卡詐欺被捕。

en: vt. to admit that something is true after trying to deny it; to give something up reluctantly; to give someone a right or privilege; vi. to admit defeat in a contest
ex: The candidate conceded defeat after losing the election.
候選人在選舉失利後承認落敗。
